assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: one transparent damage overlay for a small square arcade enemy. The reference is the rejected outer-rim version: use ONLY its charcoal-and-ivory crack material. REPLACE its composition entirely. User correction: it looks like an ornamental border, not cracking; actual branching fractures must run THROUGH THE INSIDE of the enemy face. Draw an irregular sparse network of 3 main jagged splits crossing the central area, with a few shorter forks. One prominent fissure travels from the upper-left interior diagonally through near-center toward lower-right; a second branches from left-middle through the interior toward upper-right; a third reaches from lower-middle into the center. They need not all meet at one exact point. Use angular wandering paths, variable widths, narrow dark recessed gaps, and a very thin warm ivory chipped edge. Major cracks about 2–3% of the canvas width, a few wider chips at junctions, no broad plates. This is HEAVY damage: readily visible at 32px, roughly 15–23% total coverage, with the other 77–85% genuinely transparent so colored faces and center symbols show through. The center MUST contain cracks; do NOT leave a large empty central hole. Reduce perimeter chips to just a few isolated small breaks. No line should travel around the perimeter. NO square rim, NO picture frame, NO ring, NO border, NO uniform decorative pattern. No enemy, no colored tile, no underlying square surface, no solid fill between the cracks, no floating fragments. Keep all marks inside a 5% transparent outer gutter. Crisp illustrated enamel finish, no gritty scribbles or fine noise. One square image, genuine transparent alpha background, no labels, no checkerboard. Ideally 1024x1024.

assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: one transparent HEAVY DAMAGE overlay to layer over a round red dragon tracking fireball in an arcade game. Reference image is the existing 3-stage damage atlas; use its hot orange ember edges and dark charcoal fissure colors, but REPLACE the right-hand heavy composition. User dislikes the ring-like rim: make actual cracks across the INTERIOR of the orb. Draw 3 substantial, wandering branching fractures spanning a circular footprint and crossing near the center, plus some short forks. Think a hot glowing sphere splitting across its face: dark scorched gaps with slim bright orange/cream ember edges. Several fractures MUST cross the middle; no empty central disk, no closed loop, no annulus, no concentric ring, no perimeter band. Broken irregular paths, not a geometric star or a magical rune. The entire overlay is contained in a centered disk of radius 43% of the square canvas; everything outside that disk is transparent. No circular outline. About 20–27% of the whole image is dark fissures/ember edges and the remaining area is genuinely transparent, including the spaces between cracks. Most of the red fireball beneath must remain visible. Keep most main lines 2–4% of the canvas width, with a few wider scorched junctions, strong and readable at 32px. No fireball/red fill itself, no large chunks of rock, no metallic armor, no frame, no text, no detached particles, no flames extending outside the footprint, no checkerboard. Match the crisp colorful arcade material of the reference. One square transparent sprite, NOT an atlas. Ideally 1024x1024.
